overturn_why: The clock, the year grain and the primary are right - 237 rows across 1790-2025 is one row per year. With the warehouse down neither of us can sample it. Declaring a census corruption flag a false alarm on an unverifiable assumption, at 'high' confidence, is the failure the census exists to prevent.

One of the two calls has to be wrong. I read both marts: on contracts_full the fix comment records it as a bare fiscal-year number ('2012', 1,000,000 rows per FY 2007-2026); on assistance_full it is an uncast quoted TEXT passthrough (compiled line 33) of the identical FABS/FPDS field. Resolve it as not_a_date on both, because (a) the taxonomy names a fiscal-YEAR number as the canonical not_a_date example, (b) `action_date` sits right beside it at day grain and is already primary, so the fiscal year adds zero placement power and only carries parse risk, and (c) leaving it labelled a real clock on a 19.9M-row table is an open invitation to repeat the exact bare-try_to_date bug that collapsed its twin. Medium confidence - what matters most is that the two twins stop disagreeing.

overturn_why: ACTIVE_FY is a raw TEXT passthrough and it sits directly beside ACTIVE_FQ (compiled mart lines 16-17). Together they are USASpending's data-currency stamp - 'the latest fiscal year/quarter for which this agency has submitted data' - i.e. a snapshot VINTAGE label, which the taxonomy names explicitly under not_a_date ('a version or vintage label'). It bounds no period, so span_start is wrong on its face. Worse, marking it primary puts all 111 agency rows on the shared timeline at what is a publisher bookkeeping marker, which is exactly failure mode 1 (a bookkeeping stamp charted as history). The classifier's own 'why' concedes it 'is almost certainly a single constant snapshot vintage' and that the previous census called this table clock-less - and then made it primary anyway. Confidence medium, not high: with the warehouse down I could not sample the values to prove it is constant.

overturn_why: The 'ingest' call rests on a loader note that does not apply to this table, and the note itself proves the opposite. (1) The cited script builds a DIFFERENT table: scripts/nid_dams_load.py sets SID='fed_usace_nid_dams' -> landing table FED_USACE_NID_DAMS, while the modeled staging reads source FED_NID_DAMS (library-onboarding/ripple_dbt/models/staging/fed_nid_dams/schema.yml line 8). reports/duplicate_ingest_drop_list_2026-08-10.md line 114 confirms FED_USACE_NID_DAMS is a redundant TWIN that is on the drop list. (2) In that script the file-level 'Data Last Updated' banner is a TITLE LINE that is SKIPPED before parsing (scripts/nid_dams_load.py line 38: skip = 1 if first_line.startswith('Data Last Updated') else 0), so the banner never becomes a column in any table. (3) The column that does exist is a per-row field: reports/_time_candidates.json lists DATA_LAST_UPDATED as a TEXT column of landing FED_NID_DAMS (87 cols), and the staging casts it per row as try_to_date(nullif(trim(DATA_LAST_UPDATED),''),'MM/DD/YYYY'). That is USACE's per-dam record-maintenance date - publisher-side housekeeping, exactly the same shape this same classifier labelled 'reported' for EPA FRS update_date and ICIS-Air updated_date. Calling it 'ingest' tells the index we hold Ripple's own load stamp here; we do not (that is _ingested_at, a separate column in the same staging model). Not primary either way.

Raw passthrough of TIMESTAMP sitting with the station observation fields (station_id, temperature, wind_speed), so it most likely times the observation. LOW - with a 287-row four-day API snapshot it could equally be the fetch time, so it must not anchor the table.
overturn_why: The column holds no time value. The live column scan (reports/time_index/scan.jsonl, table ENVIRONMENT.ENVIRONMENT__FED_NOAA_WEATHER_API) shows TIMESTAMP: data_type TEXT, nonnull=287 but distinct=1 with raw_min = raw_max = '' (empty string) and trusted_n=0 - every one of the 287 rows carries a blank string, and zero parse to a date. This is the COUNT(col)-looks-populated trap from CLAUDE.md: 287 non-null cells, none of them data. The station-observation half of this API pull never landed, which the same scan corroborates - EFFECTIVE is populated on all 287 rows with real alert timestamps (113 distinct, 2026-07-01T02:12:00-08:00 to 2026-07-03T00:45:00+10:00), so all 287 rows are alert rows and there are no observation rows for a TIMESTAMP to describe. Guessing 'happened' on a wholly blank column would put a phantom observation clock in the index.

The census scan settles it for this table: TIME is TEXT, 450 non-null of 450 rows, distinct=4, raw_min '2020', raw_max '2023', shape_year_only=450 - i.e. 100% of the rows are bare four-digit years, none quarterly or monthly. Year is the finest resolution this column actually supports. (Clock=happened and is_primary=true are correct and stand.)

why: raw passthrough with no cast: GDELT's event date in YYYYMMDD form; it is the true event clock and the finest one here, but it is NOT a date type - parsing it needs an explicit 'YYYYMMDD' format, and a bare parse is the documented epoch trap.
raw passthrough: the same event date in YYYYMM form - month grain by construction, and a number rather than a date.
try_to_number("YEAR") in the mart: the integer year of the event - the coarsest of GDELT's three redundant date encodings.
raw passthrough: GDELT's decimal-year float (YYYY.FFFF) encoding the same event date to roughly day precision - a NUMBER that must never be handed to a date parser, and redundant with sqldate.
raw passthrough: when GDELT added the event to its own database - the upstream publisher's clock, at or after the event, and not Ripple's ingest.
overturn_why: The census's own per-column scan (reports/time_index/scan.jsonl, REFERENCE.REFERENCE__INTL_GDELT) shows this mart column is TEXT, 1,015 non-null, 135 distinct, raw_min '' and raw_max 'VM' - and ZERO values match any date shape (shape_iso, shape_us, shape_yyyymmdd, shape_yyyymm, shape_year_only, shape_year_quarter, shape_dd_mon_yyyy all 0; trusted_n 0). 'VM' is the FIPS country code for Vietnam, and the mart (target/compiled/ripple/models/marts/reference/reference__intl_gdelt.sql) carries EXTRA_COL_0 through EXTRA_COL_20 - the raw crawl's columns are shifted, so DATEADDED holds actor/geo text, not GDELT's YYYYMMDDHHMMSS add-time. Calling it a 'reported' day-grain clock would put a country-code column on the timeline. The sibling columns are fine (SQLDATE parses 1015/1015 as YYYYMMDD), so only this column is corrupted.

overturn_why: The call itself guessed the cast might be yielding all NULLs; the census scan proves it: DATE_PUBLISHED is data_type DATE with nonnull=0 and distinct=0 across all 10 rows. try_to_date(DATE_PUBLISHED) in the mart kills every value (historical map dates are year-only or fuzzy text). why: raw passthrough of the DDR object's "DATE" field with no cast on a 25-row sample: the date of the photograph, document or interview in the Japanese American incarceration archive; unmeasured by the census because it was never typed as a date, and its text shape is unverified.
overturn_why: The census scan shows DATE is TEXT with nonnull=25 (all 25 rows) but distinct=1 and raw_min = raw_max = '' - every row holds an empty string, so a bare non-null count reads 100% populated while the column is in fact blank (the exact COUNT(col) trap the constitution warns about).
